In the last two units, you learnt two very important concepts that controls the logic of a program - Repeat until/while loops and If blocks. In this unit, we will learn a useful sensor - the Ultrasonic Distance sensor. 

Ultrasonic sensors are commonly used to measure the distance to obstacles by emitting high-frequency sound waves and detecting their echoes. 


You can use the Ultrasonic block to see the value sensed by the Ultrasonic sensor.



Ultrasonic block values are often compared using range. Below shows some examples.



Let's test out the Ultrasonic sensor.

Write a program to make the robot check and display the Ultrasonic sensor value on the LCD repeatedly.

               

1. Use Create-text-with block to convert the sensor value to text for display.
2. Short duration can make the robot more responsive.

Ultrasonic sensors are commonly used to measure the distance to obstacles by emitting high-frequency sound waves and detecting their echoes. 


You can use the Ultrasonic block to see the value sensed by the Ultrasonic sensor.



Ultrasonic block values are often compared using range. Below shows some examples.



You are creating a Distance Checker for a Facial Recognition System. The user must position his or her face within a range of 20cm to 30cm from the camera.

        

An Ultrasonic sensor is attached beside the camera. Write a program to tell the user to stay within range as follows:

1. If the Ultrasonic sensor value is more than 30cm, display "come closer" on the LCD.

2. Else if the Ultrasonic sensor value is less than 20cm, display "step back" on the LCD.

3. Otherwise, display "keep still".

4. The program will run forever.

1. Remember how you can use If block to make decisions.
2. Short duration can make the robot more responsive.

The AND block is used to combine multiple conditions.



Your code may stretch out pretty far. You can change the layout for easier viewing.
